 Daniel Nuttall from Fox Sports 18, Nov • 2m read 'I was 15': Aussie young gun fires back at reporters during tense Sandpaper exchange Share Young gun Cooper Connolly has shut down questions around the sandpaper drama engulfing Australian cricket during a tense exchange with reporters.
 Connolly, in camp with the Australian ODI squad, faced questions on Tuesday around 'Sandpapergate' which rocketed back into the news cycle following the bombshell book from former Test star Usman Khawaja.

 Talking with reporters on Tuesday, Connolly said that the sandpaper war of words involving Khawaja, David Warner, Chadd Sayers and current Test captain Pat Cummins weren't "affecting" the Australian ODI squad during their series against England.
 Connolly was in no mood to give much away in the brief 34-second exchange on the subject.
 Question - Has the sandpaper saga been discussed or affected the mood? 
 Connolly - No it hasn't affected us.
 Question - What do you make of the comments from Cummins, Warner and Sayers? 
Connolly - I don't have much to say. I was 15 at the time (of the sandpaper incident in 2018). 
 Question - Have you read the Khawaja book? 
Connolly - No.
 Question - Is ball care something the current group is being coached on? 
Connolly - No.
 Question - Do you remember it at the time when you were 15? 
 Connolly - No. I was still trying to get drafted playing AFL, so no, I don't remember much.
 The 23-year-old's comments come after former England captain Michael Vaughan called the whole situation a "s**tshow , believing it could rattle the Australian side over the course of a monster next 12 months.
 “I think it’s a s*** show,” Vaughan told foxsports.com.au.
 “None of us know. It’s just an awful look for Australian cricket.
 “It’s definitely going to have an effect going forward, without any question.
 “I think it’s bound to, the more people that people speak.”
